answers.answer: The exact JSON shape for hook entries is: `{event: [{matcher: string, hooks: [{type: 'command'|'http'|'mcp_tool'|'prompt'|'agent', command?: string, if?: string, timeout?: number, statusMessage?: string, ...}]}]}`. The five hook types are: command (shell), http (POST), mcp_tool (MCP server tool), prompt (LLM evaluation), agent (subagent). PreToolUse blocks actions by exiting with code 2 or returning JSON with `permissionDecision: 'deny'` and `permissionDecisionReason`.
answers.quote: Each hook has a `type` that determines how it runs. Most hooks use `"type": "command"`, which runs a shell command. Four other types are available: `"type": "http"`: POST event data to a URL. `"type": "mcp_tool"`: call a tool on a configured MCP server. `"type": "prompt"`: single-turn LLM evaluation. `"type": "agent"`: multi-turn verification with tool access... For `PreToolUse` permission decisions, the most restrictive answer applies, in the order `deny`, `defer`, `ask`, `allow`.

answers.answer: Permission rule syntax is: `Tool(specifier)` or bare `Tool`. Examples: Bash(npm run *), Bash(git commit *), Bash(rm *); Read(./.env), Read(~/secrets/**), Edit(/src/**); mcp__puppeteer (whole server), mcp__puppeteer__* (wildcard), mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_navigate (single tool). Rules are evaluated in order: deny takes precedence, then ask, then allow.
answers.quote: Permission rules follow the format `Tool` or `Tool(specifier)`. Bash rules match the whole command text, with `*` standing in for any text... To block Claude's file tools from reading a file or directory, add a `Read` deny rule for its path, such as `Read(./.env)` or `Read(./secrets/**)`. MCP rules use the server name as configured in Claude Code, optionally followed by the name of a tool from that server. `mcp__puppeteer` matches any tool provided by the `puppeteer` server; `mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_navigate` matches the `puppeteer_navigate` tool.

answers.answer: Rules without `paths` frontmatter are loaded at session start with the same priority as `.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Rules WITH `paths` frontmatter only load when Claude reads files matching the specified glob patterns, triggering lazy loading.
answers.quote: Rules without a `paths` field are loaded unconditionally and apply to all files. Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads files matching the pattern, not on every tool use.

answers.answer: Maximum depth for @path imports in memory files is four hops. Imports inside code spans and code blocks are ignored (parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks).
answers.quote: Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops. Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks. To mention a path in your CLAUDE.md without importing it, wrap it in backticks.

answers.answer: Size guidance: CLAUDE.md target is under 200 lines per file; files over 4 MiB are skipped entirely. Skill description cap (combined description + when_to_use) is 1,536 characters. Memory file: first 200 lines or 25KB are loaded at session start; content beyond that threshold is not loaded.
answers.quote: Size: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence... Claude Code loads a CLAUDE.md file of up to 4 MiB in full and skips a larger file... The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start.

answers.answer: Skill listing budget is calculated at 1% of the model's context window. Individual descriptions are capped at 1,536 characters (combined description + when_to_use). When context is tight, Claude Code truncates descriptions starting with skills used least frequently. Configure with `skillListingBudgetFraction` and `skillListingMaxDescChars` settings.
answers.quote: Budget scale: 1% of the model's context window... Character cap per description: 1,536 characters (combined `description` + `when_to_use`)... Adjust the budget with settings: `skillListingBudgetFraction`, `skillListingMaxDescChars`

answers.answer: Skills at `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` are discovered and available immediately as `/<name>` in the current project. Nested skills in subdirectories (like `packages/shared/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) are loaded automatically when Claude works on files in that subdirectory, and qualified variants are available (e.g., `/packages/shared:build` for nested skills that share a name with root skills).
answers.quote: Claude Code loads project skills from `.claude/skills/` in the directory where you start it and in **every parent directory up to the repository root**... **Nested skills load automatically when Claude works on files in that subdirectory**, but don't appear in the `/` menu until then.

Documented limits: questions stay open until answered; optional timeout via `askUserQuestionTimeout` setting (60s, 5m, or 10m).

answers.answer: File locations: project-scoped MCP servers in `.mcp.json` at project root; user-scoped in `~/.claude.json`. Yes, project-scoped servers from `.mcp.json` require approval before first use in interactive sessions. In non-interactive mode (`-p`), Agent SDK, cloud sessions, and bypass mode, approval is skipped and servers load automatically.
answers.quote: Project-scoped | `.mcp.json` file in project root | Yes, via version control... User-scoped | `~/.claude.json` | No, private to your user... **Yes, project-scoped servers require approval before first use** in interactive sessions... For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval in interactive sessions before using project-scoped servers from `.mcp.json` files.

answers.answer: Guidance: CLAUDE.md holds facts Claude should know in every session (coding standards, commands, conventions). If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for part of the codebase, move it to a skill or path-scoped rule. Procedures belong in skills; enforcement (hard rules that must run) belongs in hooks/permissions. Hooks and permissions enforce regardless of what Claude decides.
answers.quote: When to add to CLAUDE.md: Treat CLAUDE.md as the place you write down what you'd otherwise re-explain... Keep it to facts Claude should hold in every session: build commands, conventions, project layout, 'always do X' rules. If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for one part of the codebase, move it to a [skill] or a [path-scoped rule] instead.

answers.answer: Settings precedence (highest to lowest): Managed settings, Command line (`--settings`), Project local (`.claude/settings.local.json`), Shared project (`.claude/settings.json`), User (`~/.claude/settings.json`). A key set at a higher level overrides the same key set lower down. Array values such as permission rules merge across layers: entries from all layers combine, with higher levels taking precedence on duplicates.
answers.quote: The precedence order... Managed settings → Command line → Project local → Shared project → User. A key set at a higher level overrides the same key set lower down.
